svg.text: Configuring RDMA for NCCL, with the code: from NCCL to the firmware
The five setup steps NCCL runs when training starts, one per column. Follow a column down through the layers; each ends in a firmware command sent through the shared path at the bottom.
so the NIC may read / write it
→ dma-buf fd of the GPU buffer
Swap QP info, then step the states
in host memory, in NCCL's process
Pin GPU pages, make an MKEY
Pin the ring, create the CQ
Pin the rings, create the QP
the NIC posts a command EQE
the driver writes the input here; the firmware
DMA-reads it and DMA-writes the output
reads the command, checks it, creates or changes the object, then writes the output and status
What now exists in the NIC:
the code at that layer; indented lines are called from the line above (some steps in between are skipped)

Files: NCCL src/transport/net_ib/ (init.cc, reg.cc, connect.cc) and src/transport/net.cc; rdma-core libibverbs/ and providers/mlx5/verbs.c; Linux drivers/infiniband/core/ (uverbs_*.c) and drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/ (main.c, mr.c, cq.c, qp.c, qpc.c).
Checked against NCCL master, rdma-core master and Linux master, November 2026. After step 5 there are no more system calls: the data path is in A day in the life of an RDMA WRITE.
